chapter: Early 1930s: Bessie Smith, Rex Stewart and the Harlem scene
title: Rex Stewart as a leader
summary: Ramirez calls Rex an excellent, understanding, educated leader, temperamental only about his horn.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: He was an excellent fellow. I never knew that
he was such a human... He was real human... You know, he was very... I don't know what to say. I couldn't put it words. Very understanding with people's emotions, especially musicians, you know.

He was encouraging. A lot of things happened in those days... The only time he was temperamental was when it had to do with his horn! If he did something and it didn't come out, he'd blast at you -- he'd take out anything... But he was an educated man. Really intelligent.
He wasn't a particularly well-schooled musician, was he? I heard, you know, that he never did read too well. I don't know how true that is.
Well, I didn't have much contact with him, see. Since on the bandstand he was always the leader, he was ..(?).., you know. And I was never that close to them. But what I got from being with him...
He was a very likeable fellow. I thought he was "Ooh, ooh..." -- and really, he was a fine guy.
